## 6 Chaining and Composition

Software libraries such as OpenDP and Tumult Core [GHV20, BBD+22, SVM+] support chaining together multiple algorithms in a modular fashion to create more complex mechanisms with provable stability and privacy guarantees. Motivated by these libraries, we extend our framework to support similar functionality. Specifically, we discuss properties of timing-stable programs that are combined to create more complex functionality such as chaining and composition.

### 6.1 Chaining Timing-Stable Programs

While timing stability bounds the differences in program execution time for a single program $P$ , we are often interested in chaining together multiple programs, e.g., executing program $P_{2}$ on the output of program $P_{1}$ . For such chaining operations, we use the notation $(P_{2}\circ P_{1})(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})$ interchangeably with $P_{2}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}),\mathtt{env}_{2})$ for some execution environment $\mathtt{env}_{2}$ (see below).

#### Definition 44 (Chaining-compatible Programs).

We say that programs $P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}$ and $P_{2}:\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{E}$ are chaining-compatible if there exists a program $(P_{2}\circ P_{1})$ and a constant $c$ such that for inputs $x\in\mathcal{X}$ and environments $\mathtt{env}_{1}\in\mathcal{E}$ , there exists a (possibly random) $\mathtt{env}_{2}\in\mathcal{E}$ such that we have:

$$ \mathtt{out}((P_{2}\circ P_{1})(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=\mathtt{out}(P_{2}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})),\mathtt{env}_{2})) $$

and

$$ T_{\scriptscriptstyle(P_{2}\circ P_{1})}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})=T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})+T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})),\mathtt{env}_{2})+c. $$

Here we allow the random variable $\mathtt{env}_{2}$ to be arbitrarily correlated with $x$ , as well as the output and runtime of $P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})$ , but should be independent of the coin tosses of $P_{2}$ .

#### Remark 45.

If the construction of $P_{2}\circ P_{1}$ in the computational model does not modify the environment when chaining programs together, then $\mathtt{env}_{2}$ equals $\mathtt{out}\mathtt{env}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))$ . However, real-world systems often modify the environment before executing sequential programs, e.g., setting up CPU registers.

RAM and Word RAM programs can easily be made chaining-compatible.

#### Lemma 46.

Word RAM programs $P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}$ and $P_{2}:\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{E}$ are chaining compatible.

#### Proof.

Observe that, after $P_{1}$ ’s execution, the program’s output $y=\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))$ is located in memory locations

$$ \displaystyle M[\texttt{output\_ptr}],\dots,M[\texttt{output\_len}-1] $$

To create the chained program $P_{2}\circ P_{1}$ , we replace the HALT instruction at the end of $P_{1}$ with the instructions input_ptr = output_ptr and input_len = output_len. We then add all of the code from $P_{2}$ and adjust the necessary line numbers in any GOTO statements in the relevant $P_{2}$ code. The resulting program is an execution of $P_{2}$ on input $y$ in environment $\mathtt{env}_{2}$ that is the same as $\mathtt{out}\mathtt{env}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))$ except for these modifications to input_ptr and input_len. The total runtime is the time to execute $P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})$ , plus the execution time corresponding to the extra lines for adjusting the input pointer and input length variables, plus the time to execute $P_{2}$ on the output from $P_{1}$ in environment $\mathtt{env}_{2}$ . The proof follows similarly for RAM programs. ∎

#### Lemma 47.

Suppose $P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}$ is $(d_{1}\mapsto\{d_{2},t_{1}\})$ -jointly output/timing stable under input distance metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ and output distance metric $d_{\mathcal{Y}}$ . Similarly, suppose $P_{2}:\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{E}$ is $(d_{2}\mapsto\{d_{3},t_{2}\})$ -jointly output/timing stable under input distance metric $d_{\mathcal{Y}}$ and output distance metric $d_{\mathcal{Z}}$ . Then if $P_{1}$ and $P_{2}$ are chaining compatible, the chained program $P_{2}\circ P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{E}$ is $(d_{1}\mapsto\{d_{3},t_{1}+t_{2}\})$ -jointly output/timing stable.

#### Proof.

We show that for every $x,x^{\prime}$ satisfying $d_{\mathcal{X}}(x,x^{\prime})\leq d_{1}$ under metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ , every pair of input-compatible execution environments $\mathtt{env}_{1},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{E}$ , there exists a coupling $((\tilde{u},\tilde{v}),(\tilde{u}^{\prime},\tilde{v}^{\prime}))$ of $(\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\circ P_{1})(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})),T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}\circ P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))$ and $(\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\circ P_{1})(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime})),T_{\scriptscriptstyle(P_{2}\circ P_{1})}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{1}))$ such that $d_{\mathcal{Z}}(\tilde{u},\tilde{u}^{\prime})\leq d_{3}$ and $|\tilde{v}-\tilde{v}^{\prime}|\leq t_{1}+t_{2}$ with probability $1$ .

We construct the coupling as follows. Let $((\tilde{u}_{1},\tilde{v}_{1}),(\tilde{u}^{\prime}_{1},\tilde{v}^{\prime}_{1}))$ be the coupling associated with the joint random variables $(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})),T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))$ and $(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime})),T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}))$ satisfying $d_{\mathcal{Y}}(\tilde{u}_{1},\tilde{u}^{\prime}_{1})\leq d_{2}$ and $|\tilde{v}_{1}-\tilde{v}^{\prime}_{1}|\leq t_{1}$ with probability $1$ (by joint output/timing stability of $P_{1}$ ).

Then condition on any fixed $((u_{1},v_{1}),(u^{\prime}_{1},v^{\prime}_{1}))\in\textrm{supp}((\tilde{u}_{1},\tilde{v}_{1}),(\tilde{u}^{\prime}_{1},\tilde{v}^{\prime}_{1}))$ and execution environments $\mathtt{env}_{2}$ and $\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime}$ (conditioned on $(u_{1},v_{1})$ and $(u^{\prime}_{1},v^{\prime}_{1})$ respectively). Since $d_{\mathcal{Y}}(u_{1},u^{\prime}_{1})\leq d_{2}$ , then for every pair of execution environments $\mathtt{env}_{2},\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{E}$ , there exists a coupling $((\tilde{u}_{2},\tilde{v}_{2}),(\tilde{u}^{\prime}_{2},\tilde{v}^{\prime}_{2}))$ of the joint random variables $(\mathtt{out}(P_{2}(u_{1},\mathtt{env}_{2})),T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}(u_{1},\mathtt{env}_{2}))$ and $(\mathtt{out}(P_{2}(u_{1}^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime})),T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}(u_{1}^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime}))$ satisfying $d_{\mathcal{Z}}(\tilde{u}_{2},\tilde{u}_{2}^{\prime})\leq d_{3}$ and $|\tilde{v}_{2}-\tilde{v}^{\prime}_{2}|\leq t_{2}$ with probability $1$ (by joint output/timing stability of $P_{2}$ ).

We sample $((u_{2},v_{2}),(u^{\prime}_{2},v^{\prime}_{2}))\sim((\tilde{u}_{2},\tilde{v}_{2}),(\tilde{u}^{\prime}_{2},\tilde{v}^{\prime}_{2}))|_{\mathtt{env}_{2},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{2}}$ and set:

$$ \displaystyle(\tilde{u},\tilde{v}) \displaystyle=(u_{2},v_{1}+v_{2}+c) \displaystyle\equiv(\mathtt{out}(P_{2}(u_{1},\mathtt{env}_{2})),T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})+T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}(u_{1},\mathtt{env}_{2})+c) \displaystyle\equiv(\mathtt{out}(P_{2}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})),\mathtt{env}_{2})),T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})+T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})),\mathtt{env}_{2})+c) \displaystyle\equiv((\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\circ P_{1})(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})),T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}\circ P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})) $$

and similarly for $(\tilde{u}^{\prime},\tilde{v}^{\prime})$ , where $c$ is the chaining constant in Definition 44. It follows that:

$$ \displaystyle d_{\mathcal{Z}}(\tilde{u},\tilde{u}^{\prime})\leq d_{3} $$

and

$$ \displaystyle|\tilde{v}-\tilde{v}^{\prime}| \displaystyle=|v_{1}+v_{2}+c-v_{1}^{\prime}-v_{2}^{\prime}-c| \displaystyle=|v_{1}-v_{1}^{\prime}+v_{2}-v_{2}^{\prime}| \displaystyle\leq|v_{1}-v_{1}^{\prime}|+|v_{2}-v_{2}^{\prime}| \displaystyle\leq t_{1}+t_{2} $$

∎

#### Lemma 48.

Suppose $P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}$ is $(d_{1}\mapsto\{d_{2},t_{1}\})$ -jointly output/timing stable under input distance metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ and output distance metric $d_{\mathcal{Y}}$ . Similarly, suppose $P_{2}:\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{E}$ is $(d_{2}\mapsto t_{2})$ -OC timing stable under $d_{\mathcal{Y}}$ . Then if $P_{1}$ and $P_{2}$ are chaining compatible, the chained program $(P_{2}\circ P_{1}):\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{E}$ is $(d_{1}\mapsto t_{1}+t_{2})$ -OC timing stable.

#### Proof.

We show that for every $x,x^{\prime}$ satisfying $d_{\mathcal{X}}(x,x^{\prime})\leq d_{1}$ under metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ , every pair of input-compatible execution environments $\mathtt{env}_{1},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{E}$ , and for every $z\in\textrm{supp}((P_{2}\circ P_{1})(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))\cap\textrm{supp}((P_{2}\circ P_{1})(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}))$ , there exists a coupling $(\tilde{w},\tilde{w}^{\prime})$ of $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}\circ P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})_{|\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\circ P_{1})(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=z}$ and $T_{\scriptscriptstyle(P_{2}\circ P_{1})}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{1})_{|\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\circ P_{1})(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}))=z}$ such that $|\tilde{w}-\tilde{w}^{\prime}|\leq t_{1}+t_{2}$ with probability $1$ .

We construct the coupling as follows. Let $((\tilde{u},\tilde{v}),(\tilde{u}^{\prime},\tilde{v}^{\prime}))$ be the coupling associated with the joint random variables $(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})),T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))$ and $(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime})),T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}))$ satisfying $d_{\mathcal{Y}}(\tilde{u},\tilde{u}^{\prime})\leq d_{2}$ and $|\tilde{v}-\tilde{v}^{\prime}|\leq t_{1}$ with probability $1$ (by joint output/timing stability).

Then condition on any fixed $((u,v),(u^{\prime},v^{\prime}))\in\textrm{supp}((\tilde{u},\tilde{v}),(\tilde{u}^{\prime},\tilde{v}^{\prime}))$ and execution environments $\mathtt{env}_{2}$ and $\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime}$ (conditioned on $(u,v)$ and $(u^{\prime},v^{\prime})$ respectively). Since $d_{\mathcal{Y}}(u,u^{\prime})\leq d_{2}$ , then for every $z\in\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P_{2}(u,\mathtt{env}_{2})))\cap\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P_{2}(u^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime})))$ , there exists a coupling $(\tilde{r},\tilde{r}^{\prime})$ of the conditional runtime random variables $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}(u,\mathtt{env}_{2})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{2}(u,\mathtt{env}_{2}))=z}$ and $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}(u^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{2}(u^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime}))=z}$ satisfying $|\tilde{r}-\tilde{r}^{\prime}|\leq t_{2}$ (by output-conditional timing stability).

We sample $(r,r^{\prime})\sim(\tilde{r},\tilde{r}^{\prime})|_{\mathtt{env}_{2},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{2}}$ and set:

$$ \displaystyle\tilde{w} \displaystyle=v+r+c \displaystyle\equiv T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})+T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}(u,\mathtt{env}_{2})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{2}(u,\mathtt{env}_{2}))=z}+c \displaystyle\equiv T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})+T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})),\mathtt{env}_{2})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{2}\circ P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=z}+c \displaystyle\equiv T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}\circ P_{1}}(x)|_{P_{2}(P_{1}(x))=z} $$

and similarly for $w^{\prime}$ , where $c$ is the chaining constant in Definition 44. It follows that

$$ \displaystyle|\tilde{w}-\tilde{w}^{\prime}| \displaystyle=|u+r+c-u^{\prime}-r^{\prime}-c| \displaystyle=|u-u^{\prime}+r-r^{\prime}| \displaystyle\leq|u-u^{\prime}|+|r-r^{\prime}| \displaystyle\leq t_{1}+t_{2} $$

∎

Finally, we can chain together OC-timing-stable programs with timing-private delay programs to achieve timing privacy:

#### Theorem 49.

Let $P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}$ be $(d_{1}\mapsto t_{1})$ -OC timing stable under input distance metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ . If $P_{2}:\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}$ is a $(t_{1}\mapsto d_{2})$ -timing-private delay program with respect to privacy measure $\mathcal{M}$ , then $P_{2}\circ P_{1}$ is $(d_{1}\mapsto d_{2})$ -timing private with respect to $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ and $\mathcal{M}$ .

#### Proof.

We want to show that for all pairs of $x,x^{\prime}$ such that $d_{\mathcal{X}}(x,x^{\prime})\leq d_{1}$ , all pairs of input-compatible environments $\mathtt{env}_{1},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}$ , and all $y\in\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})))\cap\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime})))$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\mathcal{M}(T_{\scriptscriptstyle(P_{2}\circ P_{1})}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})_{|\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\circ P_{1})(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=y},T_{\scriptscriptstyle(P_{2}\circ P_{1})}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime})|_{\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\circ P_{1})(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}))=y})\leq d_{2} $$

Let $\Phi$ be the $(t_{1}\mapsto d_{2})$ -timing private delay distribution implemented by $P_{2}$ , $c$ is the chaining constant used in Definition 44, and $(\tilde{r},\tilde{r}^{\prime})$ is the coupling of the conditional random variables $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})_{|\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=y}$ and $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime})_{|\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}))=y}$ satisfying $|\tilde{r}-\tilde{r}^{\prime}|\leq t_{1}$ (by output-conditional timing stability). Let $(r,r^{\prime})\sim(\tilde{r},\tilde{r}^{\prime})$ and $\mathtt{env}_{2}$ and $\mathtt{env}_{2}$ be conditioned on $(r,y)$ and $(r^{\prime},y)$ respectively. Then,

$$ \displaystyle r+c+\Phi \displaystyle\equiv T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})_{|\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=y}+c+\phi \displaystyle\equiv T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})_{|\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=y}+c+T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}(y,\mathtt{env}_{2})_{|\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=y} \displaystyle\equiv T_{\scriptscriptstyle(P_{2}\circ P_{1})}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})_{|\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\circ P_{1})(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=y} $$

and similarly $r^{\prime}+c+\Phi\equiv T_{\scriptscriptstyle(P_{2}\circ P_{1})}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime})_{|\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\circ P_{1})(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}))=y}$ . Since $\Pr[|r-r^{\prime}|\leq t_{1}]=1$ , and $\Phi$ is a timing-private delay distribution, it follows that for $T\sim\Phi$ :

$$ \displaystyle\mathcal{M}(r+c+T,r^{\prime}+c+T)\leq d_{2} $$

and therefore

$$ \displaystyle\mathcal{M}(T_{\scriptscriptstyle(P_{2}\circ P_{1})}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})_{|\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\circ P_{1})(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=y},T_{\scriptscriptstyle(P_{2}\circ P_{1})}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime})_{|\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\circ P_{1})(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}))=y})\leq d_{2} $$

∎

We now give prove a post-processing property for programs.

#### Lemma 50 (Post-processing Program Outputs).

Let $P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}$ be $(\varepsilon,\delta)$ -differentially private program under input metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ and the smoothed max-divergence privacy measure. Let $P_{2}:\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{E}$ be a (possibly) randomized program that is output-pure (Definition 8). Then if $P_{2}$ and $P_{1}$ are chaining compatible, the chained program $P_{2}\circ P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{E}$ is $(\varepsilon,\delta)$ -differentially private under input metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ and the smoothed max-divergence privacy measure $D_{\infty}^{\delta}$ .

#### Proof.

For all adjacent inputs $x,x^{\prime}\in\mathcal{X}$ under input metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ , and all $\mathtt{env}_{1},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{E}$ , we have that $D_{\infty}^{\delta}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))||\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{1}))\leq\varepsilon$ and $D_{\infty}^{\delta}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}))||\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))\leq\varepsilon$ by the fact that $P_{1}$ is achieves $(\varepsilon,\delta)$ -differential privacy (Lemma 20). Since $P_{2}$ is output-pure, for all execution environments $\mathtt{env}_{2}\in\mathcal{E}$ , $\mathtt{out}(P_{2}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})),\mathtt{env}_{2})=f(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})))$ where $f:\mathcal{Y}\to\mathcal{Z}$ is a (possibly randomized) function. By the post-processing property for approximate DP (Lemma 22), it follows that for all $\mathtt{env}_{2},\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{E}$ :

$$ \displaystyle D_{\infty}^{\delta}(\mathtt{out}(P_{2}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})),\mathtt{env}_{2}))||\mathtt{out}(P_{2}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{1})),\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime}))) \displaystyle\hskip-284.52756pt=D_{\infty}^{\delta}(f(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})))||f(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{1})))) \displaystyle\hskip-284.52756pt\leq D_{\infty}^{\delta}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))||\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{1}))) \displaystyle\hskip-284.52756pt\leq\varepsilon $$

and similarly for $D_{\infty}^{\delta}(\mathtt{out}(P_{2}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime})),\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime}))||\mathtt{out}(P_{2}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})),\mathtt{env}_{2})))$ . ∎

#### Lemma 51.

Let $P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}$ be $(d_{in}\mapsto d_{out})$ -differentially private with respect to input distance metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ and a privacy measure $M$ . Let $P_{2}:\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}$ be a timing-private delay program such that $P_{1}$ and $P_{2}$ are chaining compatible. Then the chained program $P_{2}\circ P_{1}$ is $(d_{in}\mapsto d_{out})$ -differentially private with respect to input metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ and privacy measure $M$ .

#### Proof.

The proof follows from the fact that timing-private delay programs are output pure (Lemma 41) and Lemma 50. ∎

The post-processing property for DP (Lemma 22) states that arbitrary transformations applied to differentially private outputs produces new outputs that remain differentially private. Unfortunately, our definition of timing privacy is incompatible with post-processing. Timing privacy bounds the additional information leakage caused by observing the program’s running time after observing the program’s output. However, post-processing can potentially destroy information in the program’s output and this can result in unbounded additional information leakage in the program’s runtime.

To see this effect in action, consider a jointly output/timing-pure program $P$ implementing the identity function $f(x)=x$ with the additional property that the runtime reveals something about the input. That is, $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x)=g(x)$ for a non-constant function $g$ . Then $P$ is $(1\mapsto 0)$ -timing-private with respect to the change-one distance metric $d_{CO}$ and any privacy measure $\mathcal{M}$ (e.g., max divergence). The identity function program satisfies perfect timing privacy despite its running time being directly correlated with its input. This is due to the fact that $P$ ’s output already reveals the input and so the program’s running time reveals no additional information. However, if we apply the simple post-processing step by chaining $P$ with a deterministic, constant-time program $P^{\prime}$ that sets $\texttt{output\_len}=0$ , then the result is no longer perfectly timing-private since $\mathtt{out}((P^{\prime}\circ P)(x,\mathtt{env}))=\lambda$ 77 7 We use $\lambda$ to indicate an empty output while $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P^{\prime}\circ P}(x,\mathtt{env})$ leaks information about the input (everything about it if $g$ is injective).

*Program 4 Discrete Laplace Mechanism*

#### Lemma 52.

The Discrete Laplace Word RAM program $P:\mathbb{N}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathbb{N}\times\mathcal{E}$ (Program 4) is output-pure and timing-pure.

#### Proof.

The program only ever reads memory at location $M[\texttt{input\_ptr}]$ (line 3) to obtain the input and later writes the output to $M[0]$ . Since the program’s execution does not depend on any memory values beyond its input, then for all $y\in\mathbb{N}$ , the program’s output and runtime is identically distributed on all pairs of input-compatible execution environments $\mathtt{env},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{E}$ . ∎

#### Lemma 53.

Let $P:\mathbb{N}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathbb{N}\times\mathcal{E}$ be the Discrete Laplace program (Program 4) with scale parameter $s=1/\ln(\texttt{b}/\texttt{a})=d_{in}/\varepsilon$ . Then $P$ is $(d_{in}\mapsto\varepsilon)$ -DP with respect to input metric $d_{\mathbb{N}}(y,y^{\prime})=|y-y^{\prime}|$ and the max-divergence privacy measure.

#### Proof.

We will show that for all for $y,y^{\prime}$ satisfying $|y-y^{\prime}|\leq d_{out}$ , and all $S\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ , $\Pr[\mathtt{out}(P_{2}(y))\in S]/\Pr[\mathtt{out}(P_{2}(y^{\prime}))\in S]\leq e^{\varepsilon}$ . We ignore the execution environments in our analysis since $P$ is output-pure (Lemma 52).

The Discrete Laplace program first samples a value from a censored Discrete Laplace distribution parameterized by a shift $\mu=y$ and scale $s=1/\ln(\texttt{b}/\texttt{a})=d_{out}/\varepsilon$ . The program works similarly to Program 3 in how it samples from a Discrete Laplace distribution except that it does not bound the number of trials when sampling from a Geometric distribution (lines 14-18). Since the Word RAM model does not support values $<0$ or $>2^{\omega}-1$ , the result of $\texttt{noisy\_y}=\texttt{y}-\texttt{noise}$ (line 20) is always rounded to $0$ when $\texttt{noise}>\texttt{y}$ and the result of $\texttt{noisy\_y}=\texttt{y}+\texttt{noise}$ (line 22) is always rounded to $2^{\omega}-1$ . As a result, the program’s output is distributed as a censored Discrete Laplace random variable with PMF $f$ defined below:

$$ \displaystyle\text{$f(z|\mu=y,s=1/\ln(\texttt{b}/\texttt{a}))$}=\begin{cases}\frac{\texttt{b}-\texttt{a}}{\texttt{b}+\texttt{a}}&z=\mu\\
\frac{1}{2}\cdot\big(1-\frac{\texttt{b}-\texttt{a}}{\texttt{b}+\texttt{a}}\big)\cdot\big(\frac{\texttt{a}}{\texttt{b}}\big)^{|z-\mu|-1}\cdot\big(1-\frac{\texttt{a}}{\texttt{b}}\big)&0<z<2^{\omega},z\neq\mu\\
\frac{1}{2}\cdot\big(1-\frac{\texttt{b}-\texttt{a}}{\texttt{b}+\texttt{a}}\big)\cdot\big(\frac{\texttt{a}}{\texttt{b}}\big)^{|z-\mu|-1}&z=0\textrm{ or }z=2^{\omega}-1\\
0&\textrm{otherwise}\end{cases} $$

It follows that for all $y\in\mathcal{Y}$ :

$$ \displaystyle\Pr[\mathtt{out}(P_{2}(y))=y] \displaystyle=\frac{\texttt{b}-\texttt{a}}{\texttt{b}+\texttt{a}} \displaystyle=\frac{e^{\ln(\texttt{b}/\texttt{a})}-1}{e^{\ln(\texttt{b}/\texttt{a})}+1} \displaystyle=\frac{e^{1/s}-1}{e^{1/s}+1} \displaystyle=\frac{e^{1/s}-1}{e^{1/s}+1}\cdot e^{-|y-y|/s} $$

which matches the probability mass function for a Discrete Laplace distribution. Similarly, for all $y,z\in\mathbb{N}$ , $0<z<2^{\omega}-1,z\neq y$ :

$$ \displaystyle\Pr[\mathtt{out}(P_{2}(y))=z] \displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\cdot\big(1-\frac{\texttt{b}-\texttt{a}}{\texttt{b}+\texttt{a}}\big)\cdot\big(\frac{\texttt{a}}{\texttt{b}}\big)^{|z-y|-1}\cdot(1-\frac{\texttt{a}}{\texttt{b}}) \displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\cdot(1-\frac{e^{\ln(\texttt{b}/\texttt{a})}-1}{e^{\ln(\texttt{b}/\texttt{a})}+1})\cdot(e^{-\ln(\texttt{b}/\texttt{a})})^{(|z-y|-1)}\cdot(1-e^{-\ln(\texttt{b}/\texttt{a})}) \displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\cdot(1-\frac{e^{1/s}-1}{e^{1/s}+1})\cdot(e^{-1/s})^{(|z-y|-1)}\cdot(1-e^{-1/s}) \displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\cdot(\frac{e^{1/s}+1-e^{1/s}+1}{e^{1/s}+1})\cdot(e^{-1/s})^{(|z-y|-1)}\cdot(1-e^{-1/s}) \displaystyle=\frac{1}{e^{1/s}+1}\cdot(e^{-1/s})^{(|z-y|-1)}\cdot(1-e^{-1/s}) \displaystyle=\frac{e^{(-|z-y|+1)/s}-e^{-(|z-y|)/s}}{e^{1/s}+1} \displaystyle=\frac{e^{1/s}-1}{e^{1/s}+1}\cdot e^{-|z-y|/s} $$

Therefore, for all $y,y^{\prime}\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $|y-y^{\prime}|\leq d_{out}$ , and all $0<z<2^{\omega}-1$ , we have:

$$ \displaystyle\frac{\Pr[\mathtt{out}(P_{2}(y))=z]}{\Pr[\mathtt{out}(P_{2}(y^{\prime}))=z]} \displaystyle=\frac{e^{-|z-y|/s}}{e^{-|z-y^{\prime}|/s}} \displaystyle=e^{(|z-y^{\prime}|-|z-y|)/s} \displaystyle\leq e^{|y-y^{\prime}|/s} \displaystyle\leq e^{\varepsilon\cdot|y-y^{\prime}|/d_{out}} \displaystyle\leq e^{\varepsilon} $$

Finally for $z=2^{\omega}-1$ or $z=0$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\frac{\Pr[\mathtt{out}(P_{2}(y))=z]}{\Pr[\mathtt{out}(P_{2}(y^{\prime}))=z]} \displaystyle=\frac{(\texttt{a}/\texttt{b})^{|z-y|-1}}{(\texttt{a}/\texttt{b})^{|z-y^{\prime}|-1}} \displaystyle=\frac{e^{-\ln(\texttt{b}/\texttt{a})\cdot(|z-y|-1)}}{e^{-\ln(\texttt{b}/\texttt{a})\cdot(|z-y^{\prime}|-1)}} \displaystyle=\frac{e^{-(|z-y|-1)/s}}{e^{-(|z-y^{\prime}|-1)/s}} \displaystyle\leq e^{(|z-y^{\prime}|-|z-y|)/s} \displaystyle\leq e^{\varepsilon\cdot|y-y^{\prime}|/d_{out}} \displaystyle\leq e^{\varepsilon} $$

Therefore, for all $y,y^{\prime}$ satisfying $|y-y^{\prime}|\leq d_{out}$ , and all $S\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\frac{\Pr[\mathtt{out}(P_{2}(y))\in S]}{\Pr[\mathtt{out}(P_{2}(y^{\prime}))\in S]}\leq e^{\varepsilon} $$

and the claim is satisfied. ∎

#### Lemma 54.

Let $P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathbb{N}\times\mathcal{E}$ be the Sum Word RAM program (Program 2) and $P_{2}:\mathbb{N}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathbb{N}\times\mathcal{E}$ be the Discrete Laplace (Program 4) with scale parameter $s=1/\ln(\texttt{b}/\texttt{a})$ satisfying $\ln(\texttt{b}/\texttt{a})=\varepsilon/\Delta$ . Then the chained program $P_{2}\circ P_{1}$ is $\varepsilon$ -DP under the insert-delete distance metric $d_{\textrm{ID}}$ .

#### Proof.

The proof follows from the fact that $P_{1}$ is $(1\mapsto\Delta)$ -output stable (Lemma 29 and Lemma 75) and therefore $P_{2}\circ P_{1}$ is the Discrete Laplace mechanism executed on $\Delta$ -close inputs. The proof follows from Lemma 53. ∎

#### Lemma 55.

For any $d_{in}\in\mathbb{N}$ , the Discrete Laplace program $P:\mathbb{N}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathbb{N}\times\mathcal{E}$ (Program 4) is $(d_{in}\mapsto 5\cdot d_{in})$ -OC timing stable under the input distance metric $d_{\mathbb{N}}$ defined as $d_{\mathbb{N}}(x,x^{\prime})=|x-x^{\prime}|$ .

#### Proof.

Conditioned on $\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env}))=y$ , the program has deterministic runtime. The program’s conditional runtime $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})|_{\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env}))=y}$ is equal to $15+(5\cdot|x-y|)$ where $5\cdot|x-y|$ comes from the number of loops that are executed in lines (14-18). The other $15$ instructions are always executed on every input (lines 1-10, 2 instructions depending on the branching condition in lines 10-13, 2 instructions depending on the branching condition in lines 19-22, and lines 23-24). Therefore, for all inputs $x,x^{\prime}\in\mathbb{N}$ , conditioned on output $y\in\mathbb{N}$ ,

$$ \displaystyle|T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})|_{\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env}))=y}-T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})|_{\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env}))=y}| \displaystyle=|15+5\cdot|x-y|-15-5\cdot|x^{\prime}-y|| \displaystyle=|5\cdot(|x-y|-|x^{\prime}-y|)| \displaystyle\leq 5\cdot(|x-x^{\prime}|) \displaystyle=5\cdot d_{in} $$

∎

#### Lemma 56.

Let $P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathbb{N}\times\mathcal{E}$ be the Sum program (Program 2) and $P_{2}:\mathbb{N}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathbb{N}\times\mathcal{E}$ be the Discrete Laplace program (Program 4). Then $P_{2}\circ P_{1}$ is $(1\mapsto 3+5\Delta)$ -OC timing stable under the insert-delete distance metric $d_{\textrm{ID}}$ on the input and the output distance metric $d_{\mathbb{N}}$ defined as $d_{\mathbb{N}}(y,y^{\prime})=|y-y^{\prime}|$ .

#### Proof.

Since $P_{1}$ is $(1\mapsto\{\Delta,3\})$ -jointly output/timing stable (Lemma 29), $P_{2}$ is $(d_{in}\mapsto 5\cdot d_{in})$ -OC timing stable (Lemma 55), and $P_{1}$ is chaining compatible with $P_{2}$ (by Lemma 46), then by Lemma 48, the chained program $P_{2}\circ P_{1}$ is $(1\mapsto 3+5\cdot\Delta)$ -OC-timing stable. ∎

#### Lemma 57.

Let $P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathbb{N}\times\mathcal{E}$ be Program 2 (Sum), $P_{2}:\mathbb{N}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathbb{N}\times\mathcal{E}$ be Program 4 (Discrete Laplace) with scale parameter $s_{1}=\Delta/\varepsilon_{1}$ , and $P_{3}:\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{E}$ be Program 3 (Timing-Private Delay) with scale parameter $s_{2}=(3+5\Delta)/\varepsilon_{2}$ and shift $\mu$ . Then $P_{3}\circ(P_{2}\circ P_{1})$ is $\varepsilon_{1}$ -differentially private in its output and $(\varepsilon_{2},\delta)$ -timing private for $\delta=2\cdot e^{-\varepsilon_{2}(\mu-(3+5\Delta))/(3+5\Delta)}$ .

#### Proof.

The chained program $P_{2}\circ P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathbb{N}\times\mathcal{E}$ is $\varepsilon_{1}$ -differentially private by Lemma 54. Since $P_{3}$ is a timing-private delay program (Lemma 42) it will compute a post-processing (identity function) on the output of $P_{2}\circ P_{1}$ and by Lemma 51 the chained program $P_{3}\circ(P_{2}\circ P_{1}):\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathbb{N}\times\mathcal{E}$ is $\varepsilon_{1}$ -differentially private.

Since $P_{2}\circ P_{1}$ is $(1\mapsto 3+5\Delta)$ -OC timing stable (Lemma 56), and $P_{3}$ is a $(3+5\Delta\mapsto(\varepsilon_{2},\delta))$ -timing-private delay program for $\delta=2\cdot e^{-\varepsilon_{2}(\mu-(3+5\Delta))/(3+5\Delta)}$ (Lemma 42) under input distance metric $d_{\mathbb{N}}$ and the smoothed max-divergence privacy measure $D_{\infty}^{\delta}$ , then by Theorem 49, the chained program $P_{3}\circ(P_{2}\circ P_{1})$ is $(1\mapsto(\varepsilon_{2},\delta))$ -timing-private with respect to privacy measure $D_{\infty}^{\delta}$ . ∎

Note that Lemma 57 provides an $\varepsilon_{1}$ -DP mechanism that achieves $\varepsilon_{2}$ -timing privacy in the upper-bounded DP model when the programs are Word RAM programs. Moreover, this construction is much more efficient than the naive approach of padding execution time to the worst-case dataset size $n_{\textrm{max}}=2^{\omega}-1$ , which would result in slow runtimes for datasets with size $n<n_{\textrm{max}}$ . In the RAM model of computation, the construction yields a timing-private DP sum in the unbounded DP model.

### 6.3 Composition of Timing-Private Programs

We can treat the composition of timing-private mechanisms similarly to how we treat chaining. In particular, our framework supports the composition of timing-private programs that perform intermediate DP computations.

#### Definition 58 (Composition-compatible Programs).

We say that programs $P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y})\times\mathcal{E}$ and $P_{2}:(\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y})\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{E}$ are composition-compatible if there is a program $P_{2}\otimes P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{Z})\times\mathcal{E}$ and a constant $c$ such that for all inputs $x\in\mathcal{X}$ and all execution environments $\mathtt{env}_{1}\in\mathcal{E}$ , there exists a (possibly random) input-compatible execution environment $\mathtt{env}_{2}\in\mathcal{E}$ such that we have:

$$ \displaystyle\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\otimes P_{1})(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})),\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x,\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))),\mathtt{env}_{2}))) $$

and

$$ \displaystyle T_{\scriptscriptstyle(P_{2}\otimes P_{1})}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})=T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})+T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}((x,\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))),\mathtt{env}_{2})+c. $$

Similar to the case of chaining-compatible programs, we allow the random variable $\mathtt{env}_{2}$ to be arbitrarily correlated with the output and runtime of $P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})$ , but it should be independent of the coin tosses of $P_{2}$ .

#### Lemma 59 (Composition-compatible Word RAM Programs).

Let program $P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y})\times\mathcal{E}$ be a RAM program that writes its unmodified input to

$$ \displaystyle M[\texttt{output\_ptr}],\dots,M[\texttt{output\_ptr}+\texttt{input\_len}-1] $$

and appends the rest of its output to $M[\texttt{output\_ptr}+\texttt{input\_len}]$ , $\dots$ , $M[\texttt{output\_ptr}+\texttt{output\_len}-1]$ . Then $P_{1}$ and $P_{2}$ are composition-compatible for all programs $P_{2}:(\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y})\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{E}$ .

#### Proof.

The proof for composition-compatible programs works similarly to that of chaining-compatible programs. We replace the HALT at the end of $P_{1}$ to set $\texttt{input\_len}=\texttt{output\_len}$ and $\texttt{input\_ptr}=\texttt{output\_ptr}$ . The resulting program is an execution of $P_{2}$ on input $(x,y)$ in environment $\mathtt{env}_{2}$ that is the same as $\mathtt{out}\mathtt{env}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))$ except for these modifications to input_ptr and input_len. ∎

#### Remark 60.

The proof follows for RAM programs also.

#### Lemma 61 (Composition of OC-Timing-Stable Programs).

Let $P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y})\times\mathcal{E}$ be $(d_{1}\mapsto t_{1})$ -OC timing stable with respect to the $\mathcal{Y}$ output coordinate88 8 This means that we condition only on the $y\in\mathcal{Y}$ part of the output when considering OC-timing stability. and input distance metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ . Similarly, let $P_{2}:(\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y})\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{Z})\times\mathcal{E}$ be $(d_{1}\mapsto t_{2})$ -OC timing stable with respect to input distance metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ on its first input coordinate. If $P_{1}$ and $P_{2}$ are composition compatible, then the composed program $P_{2}\otimes P_{1}$ is $(d_{1}\mapsto t_{1}+t_{2})$ -OC timing stable.

#### Proof.

For all $x,x^{\prime}\in\mathcal{X}$ satisfying $d_{\mathcal{X}}(x,x^{\prime})\leq d_{1}$ , all input-compatible environments $\mathtt{env}_{1},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{E}$ , and all $(y,z)\in\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\otimes P_{1})(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})))\cap\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\otimes P_{1})(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime})))$ , we will construct a coupling $(\tilde{r},\tilde{r}^{\prime})$ of $T_{\scriptscriptstyle(P_{2}\otimes P_{1})}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})|_{\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\otimes P_{1})(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=(y,z)}$ and $T_{\scriptscriptstyle(P_{2}\otimes P_{1})}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime})|_{\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\otimes P_{1})(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}))=(y,z)}$ such that $|\tilde{r}-\tilde{r}^{\prime}|\leq t_{1}+t_{2}$ with probability $1$ .

Observe that for all $x,x^{\prime}\in\mathcal{X}$ such that $d_{\mathcal{X}}(x,x^{\prime})\leq d_{1}$ , all $\mathtt{env}_{1},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{E}$ , and all $(\cdot,y)\in\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})))\cap\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime})))$ , there exists a coupling $(\tilde{r}_{1},\tilde{r}_{1}^{\prime})$ of the conditional random variables $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=(x,y)}$ and $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}))=(x^{\prime},y)}$ such that $|\tilde{r}_{1}-\tilde{r}_{1}^{\prime}|\leq t_{1}$ (by the OC timing stability of $P_{1}$ ).

For all such $x,x^{\prime}$ and $\mathtt{env}_{1},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}$ , take $\mathtt{env}_{2}$ and $\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime}$ to be the execution environments satisfying:

$$ \displaystyle T_{\scriptscriptstyle(P_{2}\otimes P_{1})}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})=T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})+T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}((x,\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))),\mathtt{env}_{2})+c $$

and

$$ \displaystyle T_{\scriptscriptstyle(P_{2}\otimes P_{1})}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime})=T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime})+T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}((x^{\prime},\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}))),\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime})+c $$

respectively (such an $\mathtt{env}_{2}$ and $\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime}$ exist due to $P_{1}$ and $P_{2}$ being composition-compatible). Now fix $y\in\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})))\cap\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime})))$ . Then for all $z$ such that

$$ \displaystyle(y,z)\in\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x,y),\mathtt{env}_{2})))\cap\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x^{\prime},y),\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime}))) $$

there exists a coupling $(\tilde{r}_{2},\tilde{r}_{2}^{\prime})$ of the random variables $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}((x,y),\mathtt{env}_{2})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x,y),\mathtt{env}_{2}))=(y,z)}$ and $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}((x^{\prime},y),\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x^{\prime},y),\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime}))=(y,z)}$ such that $|\tilde{r}_{2}-\tilde{r}_{2}^{\prime}|\leq t_{2}$ (by the OC timing stability of $P_{2}$ ).

We sample $(r_{1},r_{1}^{\prime})\sim(\tilde{r}_{1},\tilde{r}_{1}^{\prime})$ and sample $\mathtt{env}_{2}$ conditioned on $(r_{1},y)$ and $\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime}$ conditioned on $(r^{\prime}_{1},y)$ . We then samlpe $(r_{2},r_{2}^{\prime})\sim(\tilde{r}_{2},\tilde{r}_{2}^{\prime})|_{\mathtt{env}_{2},\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime}}$ and let

$$ \displaystyle\tilde{r} \displaystyle=r_{1}+r_{2}+c \displaystyle=T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=y}+T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}((x,y),\mathtt{env}_{2})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x,y),\mathtt{env}_{1}))=(y,z)}+c \displaystyle=T_{\scriptscriptstyle(P_{2}\otimes P_{1})}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})|_{\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\otimes P_{1})(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=(y,z)} $$

and similarly for $\tilde{r}^{\prime}$ , where $c$ is the constant in Definition 58. It follows that

$$ \displaystyle|\tilde{r}-\tilde{r}^{\prime}| \displaystyle=|r_{1}+r_{2}+c-r_{1}^{\prime}-r_{2}^{\prime}-c| \displaystyle=|r_{1}-r_{1}^{\prime}+r_{2}-r_{2}^{\prime}| \displaystyle\leq|r_{1}-r_{1}^{\prime}|+|r_{2}-r_{2}^{\prime}| \displaystyle\leq t_{1}+t_{2} $$

∎

Lemma 61 shows that we can reason about timing stability when composing DP programs. After analyzing the timing stability of the overall composed program, we can add a single timing delay to protect the release from timing attacks. Alternatively, we can compose timing-private programs such that composed program is also timing-private.

#### Lemma 62 (Composition of Timing-Private Programs).

Let $\mathcal{C}:(\mathcal{M}\times\mathcal{M})\to\mathcal{M}$ be a valid composition function for a privacy measure $M$ ; meaning that if $M(X_{1},X^{\prime}_{1})\leq d_{1}$ and $M(X_{2}|X_{1}=x,X^{\prime}_{2}|X^{\prime}_{1}=x^{\prime})\leq d_{2}$ then $M((X_{1},X_{2}),(X^{\prime}_{1},X^{\prime}_{2}))\leq C(d_{1},d_{2})$ . Let $P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y})\times\mathcal{E}$ be $(d_{0}\mapsto d_{1})$ -timing private with respect to its second output coordinate, input metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ , and privacy measure $M$ . Let $P_{2}:(\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y})\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{Z})\times\mathcal{E}$ be $(d_{0}\mapsto d_{2})$ -timing private with respect to its second output coordinate, input metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ , and privacy measure $M$ . If $P_{1}$ and $P_{2}$ be composition compatible, then $P_{1}\otimes P_{2}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{Z})\times\mathcal{E}$ is $(d_{0}\mapsto C(d_{1},d_{2}))$ -timing-private with respect to $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ and privacy measure $M$ .

#### Proof.

By composition-compatibility, for all $x\in\mathcal{X}$ and input-compatible execution environments $\mathtt{env}_{1}$ , there exists an input-compatible execution environment $\mathtt{env}_{2}$ such that

$$ \displaystyle T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}\otimes P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})=T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})+T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}((x,\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))),\mathtt{env}_{2})+c $$

We can therefore analyze $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}\otimes P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})|_{\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\otimes P_{1})(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})=(y,z)}$ using the joint random variable:

$$ \displaystyle(T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=(x,y)},T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}((x,y),\mathtt{env}_{2})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x,y),\mathtt{env}_{2}))=(y,z)}) $$

and similarly for $x^{\prime}$ . Since $P_{1}$ is timing-private with respect to input metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ and privacy measure $M$ , it follows that for all $d_{1}$ -close inputs $x,x^{\prime}\in\mathcal{X}$ , all input-compatible execution environments $\mathtt{env}_{1},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{1}$ , and all $y\in\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})))\cap\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{1})))$

$$ \displaystyle M(T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=(x,y)},T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{1})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{1}))=(x^{\prime},y)})\leq d_{1} $$

Similarly, since $P_{2}$ is timing-private with respect to input metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ and privacy measure $M$ , it follows that for all inputs $(x,y),(x^{\prime},y)\in\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}$ that are $d_{1}$ -close on their first coordinate, all input-compatible execution environments $\mathtt{env}_{2},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{2}$ , and all $(y,z)\in\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x,y),\mathtt{env}_{2})))\cap\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x^{\prime},y),\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{2})))$

$$ \displaystyle M(T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}((x,y),\mathtt{env}_{2})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x,y),\mathtt{env}_{2}))=(y,z)},T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}((x^{\prime},y),\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{2})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x^{\prime},y),\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{2}))=(y,z)})\leq d_{2} $$

Let

$$ \displaystyle Y=T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=(x,y)} \displaystyle Y^{\prime}=T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{1})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{1}))=(x^{\prime},y)} \displaystyle Z=T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}((x,y),\mathtt{env}_{2})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x,y),\mathtt{env}_{2}))=(y,z)} \displaystyle Z^{\prime}=T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}((x^{\prime},y),\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{2})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x^{\prime},y),\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{2}))=(y,z)} $$

Then

$$ \displaystyle M((Y,Z),(Y^{\prime},Z^{\prime})) \displaystyle\leq C(M(Y,Y^{\prime}),M(Z,Z^{\prime})) \displaystyle\leq C(d_{1},d_{2}) $$

which is what we wanted to show. ∎

The above composition theorem says that we can compose timing-private programs and keep track of the overall timing privacy guarantees. For example, $C((\varepsilon_{1},\delta_{1}),(\varepsilon_{2},\delta_{2}))=(\varepsilon_{1}+\varepsilon_{2},\delta_{1}+\delta_{2})$ is a valid composition function for approximate-DP (Lemma 23). Lemma 62 says that the composition of a program $P_{1}$ that is $(\varepsilon_{1},\delta_{1})$ -timing private with a program $P_{2}$ that is $(\varepsilon_{2},\delta_{2})$ -timing private, results in a new program that is $(\varepsilon_{1}+\varepsilon_{2},\delta_{1}+\delta_{2})$ -timing private.

We can use the above fact to construct timing-private programs, for example, that compute DP means from a timing-private DP sum program and a timing-private DP count program. The DP sum and DP count can be interpreted as the numerator and denominator of the mean, respectively. For example, Program 5 accepts as input $(x,y)$ where $x$ is a dataset and $y$ is a DP sum over $x$ . By chaining together Program 5 with a (modified) Program 4, we obtain a program that outputs a DP sum followed by a DP count.

Input: A dataset $x$ occupying memory locations $M[0],\dots,M[\texttt{input\_len}-2]$ and a value $y\in\mathbb{N}$ at memory location $M[\texttt{input\_len}-1]$ . The value $y$ can be a (possibly DP) sum over the elements $M[0],\dots,M[\texttt{input\_len}-1]$ , for example.

Output: The value $y$ and the size of the dataset $\texttt{input\_len}-1$ .

```
1: $\texttt{output\_ptr}=\texttt{input\_len}-2$ ;
2: $\texttt{output\_len}=2$ ;
3: $M[\texttt{output\_ptr}+1]=\texttt{input\_len}-1$ ;
4: HALT;
```

*Program 5 Dataset Count Program*

### 6.4 A Timing Private Unbounded Mean

We now give an example of how one can use composition-compatible programs to compute timing-private DP means in the unbounded DP model.

#### Remark 63.

In the following constructions, we will assume a modified version of the timing-private DP sum program from Lemma 57 that instead writes its output in a composition-compatible way (by appending its output to the end of its input and setting output_ptr and output_len accordingly). This is a straight-forward modification that involves updating Program 2 and Program 4 so that the original input is included in the chained program’s output. Similarly, when we chain together Program 4 with Program 5, we will assume a modified version of the Discrete Laplace program that accepts as input $(y_{1},y_{2})$ and outputs $(y_{1},y_{2}+\eta)$ where $\eta$ is the noise drawn from the Discrete Laplace distribution. We note that these changes can be made such that the stability claims for Lemma 55 and Lemma 29 continue to hold by ensuring that the modifications incur some constant additive overhead to the runtime.

#### Lemma 64.

The Dataset Count program $P:(\mathcal{X}\times\mathbb{N})\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})\times\mathcal{E}$ (Program 5) is $(d_{in}\to\{d_{in},0\})$ -jointly output/timing stable under the output distance metric $d_{\mathbb{N}}$ on the second output coordinate of $(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})$ and the input distance metric $d_{\textrm{ID}}$ .

#### Proof.

The program always executes in $4$ instructions and is therefore $(d_{in}\mapsto 0)$ -timing stable under the input distance metric $d_{\textrm{ID}}$ (Lemma 70). If you add or remove a row from the dataset $x\in\mathcal{X}$ , then the count changes by at most $d_{in}$ . Therefore, the program is $(d_{in}\mapsto d_{in})$ -output stable (with respect to its second output coordinate) under the output distance metric $d_{\mathbb{N}}$ and input metric $d_{\textrm{ID}}$ . Since the program is deterministic in its output, the program satisfies $(d_{in}\mapsto\{d_{in},0\})$ -joint output/timing stability (Lemma 28). ∎

#### Lemma 65.

Let $P_{1}:(\mathcal{X}\times\mathbb{N})\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})\times\mathcal{E}$ be the Dataset Count program (Program 5) and $P_{2}:(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})\times\mathcal{E}$ be the Discrete Laplace program (Program 4) modified according to Remark 63 with $s=1/\varepsilon_{2}=1/\ln(\texttt{b}/\texttt{a})$ . Then $P_{2}\circ P_{1}:(\mathcal{X}\times\mathbb{N})\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})\times\mathcal{E}$ is $\varepsilon_{2}$ -differentially private under the max-divergence privacy measure with respect to the 2nd coordinate of $(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})$ and the input distance $d_{\textrm{ID}}$ .

#### Proof.

$P_{1}$ is $(d_{in}\mapsto d_{in})$ -output stable with respect to input distance metric $d_{\textrm{ID}}$ and output distance metric $d_{\mathbb{N}}$ on the second output coordinate of $(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})$ (Lemma 64 and Lemma 75). Therefore the proof follows exactly by Lemma 53 since $P_{2}\circ P_{1}$ is the Discrete Laplace program executed on $d_{in}$ -close inputs under the input distance $d_{\mathbb{N}}(n,n^{\prime})=|n-n^{\prime}|$ . ∎

#### Lemma 66.

Let $P_{1}:(\mathcal{X}\times\mathbb{N})\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})\times\mathcal{E}$ be the Dataset Count program (Program 5), and $P_{2}:(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})\to(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})\times\mathcal{E}$ be the Discrete Laplace program (Program 4) modified according to Remark 63. Then the chained program $P_{2}\circ P_{1}:(\mathcal{X}\times\mathbb{N})\to(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})\times\mathcal{E}$ is $(d_{in}\mapsto 5\cdot d_{in})$ -OC timing stable under the insert-delete distance metric $d_{\textrm{ID}}$ .

#### Proof.

The dataset count program is constant-time and therefore $(d_{in}\mapsto\{d_{in},0\})$ -jointly output/timing stable under $d_{\textrm{ID}}$ . By Lemma 55 and Lemma 48, we have that the chained program is $(d_{in}\mapsto 5\cdot d_{in})$ -OC timing stable under $d_{\textrm{ID}}$ . ∎

#### Lemma 67.

Let $P_{1}:(\mathcal{X}\times\mathbb{N})\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})\times\mathcal{E}$ be the Dataset Count program (Program 5), and $P_{2}:(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})\to(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})\times\mathcal{E}$ be the Discrete Laplace program (Program 4) modified according to Remark 63, with scale parameter $s_{1}=1/\varepsilon_{1}$ . Let $P_{3}:\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{E}$ be Program 3 (Timing-Private Delay) with scale parameter $s_{2}=5/\varepsilon_{2}$ and shift $\mu$ . Then $P_{3}\circ(P_{2}\circ P_{1})$ is $\varepsilon_{1}$ -differentially private in its output and $(\varepsilon_{2},\delta)$ -timing private for $\delta=2\cdot e^{\varepsilon_{2}(\mu-5)/5}$ .

#### Proof.

The chained program $P_{2}\circ P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathbb{N}\times\mathcal{E}$ is $\varepsilon_{1}$ -differentially private by Lemma 65. Since $P_{3}$ is a timing-private delay program (Lemma 42) it will compute a post-processing (identity function) on the output of $P_{2}\circ P_{1}$ and by Lemma 51 the chained program $P_{3}\circ(P_{2}\circ P_{1}):\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathbb{N}\times\mathcal{E}$ is $\varepsilon_{1}$ -differentially private.

Since $P_{2}\circ P_{1}$ is $(1\mapsto 5)$ -OC timing stable (Lemma 66), and $P_{3}$ is a $(5\mapsto(\varepsilon_{2},\delta))$ -timing-private delay program for $\delta=2\cdot e^{-\varepsilon_{2}(\mu-5)/5}$ (Lemma 42) under input distance metric $d_{\mathbb{N}}$ and the smoothed max-divergence privacy measure $D_{\infty}^{\delta}$ , then by Theorem 49, the chained program $P_{3}\circ(P_{2}\circ P_{1})$ is $(1\mapsto(\varepsilon_{2},\delta))$ -timing-private with respect to privacy measure $D_{\infty}^{\delta}$ . ∎

#### Lemma 68.

Let $P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y})\times\mathcal{E}$ be the $\varepsilon_{1}$ -DP and $(\varepsilon_{2},\delta)$ -timing-private sum program (Lemma 57) that has been modified according to Remark 63. Let $P_{2}:(\mathcal{X}\times\mathbb{N})\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})\times\mathcal{E}$ be the $\varepsilon_{1}$ -DP and $(\varepsilon_{2},\delta)$ -timing-private dataset count program (Lemma 67). Then $P_{1}$ and $P_{2}$ are composition-compatible.

#### Proof.

Observe that, due to the modifications from Remark 63, $P_{1}$ writes to its output the original dataset $x\in\mathcal{X}$ followed by the DP sum $y\in\mathbb{N}$ . By Lemma 59 the claim follows. ∎

#### Lemma 69.

Let $P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y})\times\mathcal{E}$ be the $\varepsilon_{1}$ -DP and $(\varepsilon_{2},\delta)$ -timing-private sum program (Lemma 57) that has been modified according to Remark 63. Let $P_{2}:(\mathcal{X}\times\mathbb{N})\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})\times\mathcal{E}$ be the $\varepsilon_{1}$ -DP and $(\varepsilon_{2},\delta)$ -timing-private dataset count program (Lemma 67). Then $P_{2}\otimes P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})\times\mathcal{E}$ is $2\varepsilon_{1}$ -DP and $(2\varepsilon_{2},2\delta)$ -timing-private.

#### Proof.

The first output coordinate of $P_{2}\otimes P_{1}$ is the output of $P_{1}$ , and the second output coordinate of $P_{2}\otimes P_{1}$ is the output of $P_{2}$ . Since $P_{1}$ is $\varepsilon_{1}$ -DP under input metric $d_{\textrm{ID}}$ and output metric $d_{\mathbb{N}}$ (Lemma 54), and $P_{2}$ is $\varepsilon_{1}$ -DP under input metric $d_{\textrm{ID}}$ and output metric $d_{\mathbb{N}}$ (Lemma 65), it follows that for all $x,x^{\prime}\in\mathcal{X}$ satisfying $d_{\textrm{ID}}(x,x^{\prime})\leq 1$ , all input-compatible $\mathtt{env}_{1},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{1},\mathtt{env}_{2},\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{E}$ , and all $(S_{1},S_{2})\subseteq(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})$ :

$$ \displaystyle\Pr[\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\otimes P_{1})(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))\in(S_{1},S_{2})] \displaystyle\hskip-150.0pt=\Pr[\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))\in S_{1}]\cdot\Pr[\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x,\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))),\mathtt{env}_{2}))\in S_{2}] \displaystyle\hskip-150.0pt\leq e^{\varepsilon_{1}}\cdot\Pr[\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}))\in S_{1}]\cdot e^{\varepsilon_{2}}\cdot\Pr[\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x^{\prime},\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}))),\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime}))\in S_{2}] \displaystyle\hskip-150.0pt\leq e^{\varepsilon_{1}+\varepsilon_{2}}\cdot\Pr[\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\otimes P_{1})(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}))\in(S_{1},S_{2})] $$

Therefore, $P_{2}\otimes P_{1}$ is $2\varepsilon_{1}$ -DP with respect to input metric $d_{\textrm{ID}}$ and the max-divergence privacy measure. The claim that $P_{2}\otimes P_{1}$ is $(2\varepsilon_{2},2\delta)$ -timing-private follows from the fact that $P_{1}$ is $(\varepsilon_{2},\delta)$ -timing-private, $P_{2}$ is $(\varepsilon_{2},\delta)$ -timing-private, and Lemma 62 and letting $C((\varepsilon,\delta),(\varepsilon,\delta))=(2\varepsilon,2\delta)$ be the composition function by Lemma 23. ∎

## 7 Implementation

A proof-of-concept implementation of our framework on top of the OpenDP library in available in the Github repository [SVM+]. The proof of concept supports defining timing stability maps for transformations and output-conditional timing stability maps for measurements. We additionally implemented a proof-of-concept timing-private delay function that can be chained with arbitrary output-conditional timing stable measurements to delay their output release.

The purpose of the implementation is to illustrate the compatibility of our framework with existing differential privacy libraries, not to claim that the implementation provides timing privacy for physical executions. As discussed in Section 1.2, we leave for future work the problem of instantiating our framework for physical timing channels, which would involve constraining the execution environment, identifying the appropriate units to measure timing, and finding realistic upper bounds on actual timing-stability constants.

## Appendix A Stability Proofs

#### Lemma 70.

A program $P:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}$ is $(d_{in}\mapsto 0)$ -timing-stable if for all pairs of inputs $x,x^{\prime}\in\mathcal{X}$ , and all input-compatible execution environments $\mathtt{env},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{E}$ , $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})\equiv T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime})$ .

#### Proof.

For any two inputs $x$ and $x^{\prime}$ , take the coupling $(\tilde{r},\tilde{r}^{\prime})$ to be $(T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env}),T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env}))$ . Since $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})\equiv T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime})$ , it follows that the marginal distributions of $\tilde{r}$ and $\tilde{r}^{\prime}$ are identical to $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})$ and $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime})$ , and $|\tilde{r}-\tilde{r}^{\prime}|=0$ . ∎

#### Lemma 71.

If $P:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}$ satisfies for all $x\in\mathcal{X}$ , $\mathtt{env}\in\mathcal{E}$ , $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})=c$ for some constant $c$ , then $P$ is $(d_{in}\mapsto 0)$ -timing stable.

#### Proof.

Since $P$ is constant time, $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})=c$ for all $x$ and $\mathtt{env}$ , then for all $x,x^{\prime}$ and input-compatible $\mathtt{env},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}$ , $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})\equiv T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime})$ and the claim follows from Lemma 70. ∎

#### Lemma 72.

If $P:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}$ is deterministic (in its output) and is $(d_{in}\mapsto t_{out})$ -timing stable, then $P$ is $(d_{in}\mapsto t_{out})$ -OC-timing stable.

#### Proof.

For all $x$ and $x^{\prime}$ satisfying $d_{\mathcal{X}}(x,x^{\prime})\leq d_{in}$ , and any pair of environments $\mathtt{env},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{E}$ , either $\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env}))\neq\mathtt{out}(P(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}))$ or $\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env}))=\mathtt{out}(P(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}))$ . If $\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env}))\neq\mathtt{out}(P(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}))$ , then there is no requirement on the distributional closeness of $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})$ and $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime})$ and the claim is satisfied. Now suppose that $\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env}))=\mathtt{out}(P(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}))=y$ . By the timing stability of $P$ there exists a coupling $(\tilde{r},\tilde{r}^{\prime})$ of the random variables $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})$ and $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime})$ such that $|\tilde{r}-\tilde{r}^{\prime}|\leq t_{out}$ . Since $P$ is deterministic it also follows that $\tilde{r}$ and $\tilde{r}^{\prime}$ have the same marginal distributions as $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})_{|\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env}))=y}$ and $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x^{\prime})_{|\mathtt{out}(P(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}))=y}$ respectively, and the claim holds. ∎

#### Lemma 73.

If $P:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}$ has constant runtime then $P$ is $(d_{in}\to 0)$ -OC timing stable.

#### Proof.

Since $P$ is constant time, $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})=c$ for all $x$ and $\mathtt{env}$ . For all $y\in\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env})))\cap\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime})))$ with $d_{\mathcal{X}}(x,x^{\prime})\leq d_{in}$ , let the coupling $(\tilde{r},\tilde{r}^{\prime})$ of $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})_{|\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env}))=y}$ and $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime})_{|\mathtt{out}(P(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}))=y}$ take the value $(c,c)$ . Then $\tilde{r}$ and $\tilde{r}^{\prime}$ are identically distributed to $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})_{|\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env}))=y}$ and $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime})_{|\mathtt{out}(P(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}))=y}$ respectively, and $|\tilde{r}-\tilde{r}^{\prime}|=|c-c|=0$ . ∎

#### Lemma 74.

Jointly output/timing-stable programs are timing-stable programs.

#### Proof.

If $P:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}$ is $(d_{in}\mapsto\{d_{out},t_{out}\})$ -jointly output/timing stable with respect to input metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ , then for every $x,x^{\prime}\in\mathcal{X}$ satisfying $d_{\mathcal{X}}(x,x^{\prime})\leq d_{in}$ and all pairs of execution environments $\mathtt{env},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{E}$ , there exists a coupling $((\tilde{u},\tilde{r}),(\tilde{u}^{\prime},\tilde{r}^{\prime}))$ of the joint random variables $(\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env})),T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env}))$ and $(\mathtt{out}(P(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime})),T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}))$ satisfying $\Pr[|\tilde{r}-\tilde{r}^{\prime}|<t_{out}]=1$ . Take $(\tilde{r},\tilde{r}^{\prime})$ to be the coupling of the random variables $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})$ and $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime})$ and the claim follows. ∎

#### Lemma 75.

Jointly output/timing-stable programs are output-stable programs.

#### Proof.

If $P:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}$ is $(d_{in}\mapsto\{d_{out},t_{out}\})$ -jointly output/timing stable with respect to input metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ and output metric $d_{\mathcal{Y}}$ , then for every $x,x^{\prime}\in\mathcal{X}$ satisfying $d_{\mathcal{X}}(x,x^{\prime})\leq d_{in}$ and all pairs of execution environments $\mathtt{env},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{E}$ , there exists a coupling $((\tilde{u},\tilde{r}),(\tilde{u}^{\prime},\tilde{r}^{\prime}))$ of the joint random variables $(\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env})),T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env}))$ and $(\mathtt{out}(P(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime})),T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}))$ satisfying $d_{\mathcal{Y}}(\tilde{u},\tilde{u}^{\prime})\leq d_{out}$ with probability $1$ . Take $(\tilde{u},\tilde{u}^{\prime})$ to be the coupling of the random variables $\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env}))$ and $\mathtt{out}(P(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}))$ and the claim follows. ∎
